Our story

Through it all,we kept going.

From private kitchens in New York, through the hardest season of our lives, to a little pink cottage in Lake Mary. This is how Donutste was made.

Scroll

Before the pink cottage, before the lines and before anyone knew the name Donutste, there were two chefs who believed that whatever you make with your hands carries an intention.

I
New York · 2013 – 2019

The private chefs.

Meditating Chef & CoChef Shalom & Chef Victoria

Chef Shalom built Meditating Chef & Co in New York, leading a team of five and cooking private dinners for homes, celebrities and companies. Chef Victoria cooked beside him for close to a decade before we ever started a company together.

Our food reached the late Toni Morrison, The Breakfast Club, NFL players, the executive team at Moncler and the kitchens of New York Fashion Week. We were trained to think like chefs in everything: balance, technique and the feeling a guest leaves with. Years later, all of that would be folded into our donuts, doughssants, cinnamon rolls and pastries.

II · The hardest season

There was a season we had no home of our own.

We kept going.

Every morning, God gave us the strength to rise.

We didn’t have a storefront, a team or a safety net. We had our hands, our training and a recipe we refused to give up on. Out of that season came ArtisaDough, a plant-based dough company, and the donuts, doughssants, cinnamon rolls and pastries the world now knows as Donutste.

We share this part because someone reading it is in their own hard season. Keep going. Keep making things with love.

As told on Spectrum News 13, Florida Inspires · “From homeless to donuts”
III
New York & New Jersey · 2019 – 2022

The underground.

ArtisaDoughWord of mouth

With no sign and no shop, our donuts found their way onto shelves across the city. People tasted them, asked where they came from and traced them back to us. It became a quiet cult following, passed from one person to the next.

That was when people started calling it the best donut in the world. We never stopped believing it.

IV
Florida · 2022

Under the pink tent.

Donutste is bornStarting over

We came to Florida and started again, one market at a time: Lake Mary, Mount Dora, and pop-ups in Winter Park, Orlando and all across Central Florida. We set up the pink tent with our son, carried in bins of hundreds of donuts and watched the line form before we were even open.

ArtisaDough stopped being a dough and became a name: Donutste. And to everyone who found us, we said: Welcome home.

Chef Shalom quickly attained cult status in markets around Central Florida, where their plant-based donuts spread through word of mouth.
Sanford Herald · March 2023
V
Lake Mary · 2023 – 2024

The pink cottage.

Our first shopBest Donuts In The World

The tent couldn’t hold the lines anymore, so we opened a little pink cottage in Lake Mary. Out front, a sidewalk sign said what we had believed since New York: Best Donuts In The World.

In January 2024, an Orlando food blogger named us the best donuts in Central Florida and more than a million people watched. The lines wrapped around the cottage, and we worked with the City of Lake Mary on a pre-order plan so everyone could still get a box.

VI
Today

Welcome home.

Lake Mary, FloridaThe first Black-owned bakery in Lake Mary

Today Donutste bakes from our own commercial kitchen in Lake Mary, the first Black-owned bakery in the city. We’ve been on FOX 35, Spectrum News 13 and Telemundo 31, in the Orlando Sentinel, Visit Orlando, VegNews and VegOut, and our Doughssant went viral.

It’s still the two of us, making every donut, doughssant, cinnamon roll and pastry by hand, the same way we did when we had nothing. Every box carries that story. Thank you for being part of it.

Together, he and his wife, Chef Victoria, have created magic with their baked goods.
Visit Orlando · February 2026
